title: Microsoft Teams: AI-generated meeting memory for knowledge retention
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents meeting-memory PowerShell parameters, contrary to the briefing's claim that none are documented; the reference warns that the feature is not fully released and the setting currently has no effect. The retention automation also links to a reference that does not document the rule command printed in that control. The default, retention period and revised rollout sequence are supported.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls prose and table
claims.claim: No cmdlet parameter for the meeting memory policy setting is documented.
claims.quote: -AllowMeetingKnowledgeGeneration: This setting allows admins to control whether an AI-generated meeting knowledge file is created for meetings organized by the user. This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api.kind to 'powershell', call to 'Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy> -AllowMeetingKnowledgeGeneration <Boolean>', and docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/teams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy; mirror this in the rendered table. Replace the prose absence assertion with 'PowerShell documents -AllowMeetingKnowledgeGeneration, but its reference warns that the feature is not fully released and the setting currently has no effect.' Add that same warning to the control note; do not describe this as an effective pre-release switch.

claims.claim: The memory setting offers On for all meetings, Only for meetings with transcription, and Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy> -Copilot supports Enabled, EnabledWithTranscript, EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn and Disabled.
claims.quote: On | Enabled; On with saved transcript required | EnabledWithTranscript; On with transcript saved by default | EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn; Off | Disabled
claims.fix: Add a qualification to this control note: 'The Copilot management guide lists these four values; the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference currently lists only Enabled and EnabledWithTranscript.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/teams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy for that reference discrepancy.

claims.claim: A retention policy can be created through Purview > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies. 2. Select New retention policy

claims.claim: The linked New-RetentionCompliancePolicy reference documents the entire printed policy-and-rule retention sequence.
claims.quote: Searched: New-RetentionComplianceRule, RetentionDuration and RetentionComplianceAction in the cited New-RetentionCompliancePolicy reference. It links to the separate rule reference but does not document the rule's parameters; both references were opened.
claims.fix: Keep the complete, separately cited policy-and-rule procedure in the prose. In controls[3].api and its rendered cell, use only 'New-RetentionComplianceRule -Name <rule> -Policy <existing-policy> -RetentionDuration <days> -RetentionComplianceAction <Keep|Delete|KeepAndDelete>' and set docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-retentioncompliancerule?view=exchange-ps. Change the note to 'Security & Compliance PowerShell. Requires an existing policy scoped to the memory container URL.' This makes the table call and its single reference agree without adding a row.

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy in Security & Compliance PowerShell needs a location and a rule before the policy is valid.
claims.quote: Policies are not valid until a rule is added (for retention policies) or a label is added (for retention label policies). ... at least one location parameter must be defined to create a retention policy or retention label policy.

claims.claim: New-RetentionComplianceRule accepts Delete, Keep and KeepAndDelete as retention actions.
claims.quote: The RetentionComplianceAction parameter specifies the retention action for the rule. Valid values are: Delete Keep KeepAndDelete

claims.claim: The retention rule's RetentionDuration parameter can specify a duration in days.
claims.quote: The RetentionDuration parameter specifies the hold duration for the retention rule. Valid values are: An integer: The hold duration in days.
